outcomes: Registry downloads of one process authenticate through the workspace's credential provider when the user turns it on
A bearer reaches only the hosts its credential names, fetched once per purpose while it is valid
A workspace without a provider, or a process without the flag, keeps its host-keyed credentials
nonGoals: Serving read credentials for npm, Go or container registries, or any credential to an extension process, through the provider in this release
A runner provider that echoes invocation-providers-v1; the Putnami Cloud runner provider moves to it separately

requirements.text: The credential provider is off unless --providers, or PUTNAMI_PROVIDERS when the flag is absent, names install or publish; an unknown value is a usage error naming its source. The choice holds for one process: the CLI removes PUTNAMI_PROVIDERS from what it starts. A bound execution request enables exactly its invocation.providers, except publish when it carries no invocation.publication. --where remote with providers is refused before submission unless the runner provider echoes invocation-providers-v1.

The provider is the one loaded extension that declares the credential-provider command. With none, every download keeps its host-keyed credential and nothing is launched. With two, the first download that needs the credential fails naming both extensions and the source of the choice, and a command that downloads nothing still runs.

The provider starts on the first download that needs a credential, or before the first hook when publish is enabled, and is asked at most once per purpose while the answer is valid, however many hosts and concurrent requests need it. The bearer is sent only to a host and port the credential names; any other host keeps its host-keyed credential. A credential is fetched again before it expires, at most a minute early and at most halfway through its lifetime. No bearer is written to any output.

A refusal fails every request of its purpose, whatever its host, with its code, and holds for the process; absence serves nothing and holds too. The CLI never retries a refused or failed request with another credential. A crash, timeout, malformed answer or failed start fails the request and answers for 30 s; the first request after that asks again, restarting an exited or hung provider. An answer written just before the provider exits is still read.
